memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses told Aaron, 'Say to the entire Israelite community, "Come before the
LORD, for he has heard your grumbling."' While Aaron was speaking to the whole
Israelite community, they looked toward the desert, and there was the glory of
the LORD appearing in the cloud." - Ex 16:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Come before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling."

That is an extraordinary invitation. God does not say, "Sort yourselves out and
then approach." He calls them to come, and the stated reason is that He has
heard their complaining.

We would expect the opposite. Surely you clean up before you come near. But this
is how God consistently works. He calls people as they are, and the coming is
where the change begins.

Hebrews says we may "approach God's throne of grace with confidence, so that we
may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need" (Heb 4:16).
Notice the word "confidence," and notice that we come in the time of need, not
after we have sorted the need out.

Then they look toward the desert, and the glory of the LORD appears in the
cloud.

The glory was in the desert. Not back at Elim with the palm trees, and not ahead
in the promised land. In the barren place where they were hungry and
complaining.

Do not assume God's glory belongs only to your better seasons. It often shows up
in the wilderness.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you feel you must be in a good spiritual state before approaching God?
2. Where have you seen God most clearly, in comfort or in difficulty?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You call me to come even when I have been complaining.
Show me Your glory here, in the place I would rather not be. Amen.
